one_liner: Pure-Rust Opus encoder, decoder and Ogg container with hand-written SIMD; encodes 1.09-1.76x as fast as libopus 1.6.1 on an M1 Pro.
what_it_does: A dependency-free Rust crate (no C, FFI or build.rs) that encodes and decodes Opus (RFC 6716) in SILK, CELT and hybrid modes at 8-48 kHz, mono and stereo, at all nine frame sizes. It also reads and writes Ogg Opus files (RFC 7845). The API mirrors libopus semantics with Rust types: OpusEncoder::new(rate, channels, Application) with public setting fields (bitrate_bps, complexity, rate_control, FEC, DTX), encode/encode_s16 into a caller-sized packet buffer, and OpusDecoder::decode/decode_s16, where an empty packet triggers concealment. Extras are multistream up to 7.1, a repacketizer, packet inspection without decoding, a Trim helper for pre-skip and end-trim, and chunk-parallel encode_parallel. There is no C ABI, so it is not a drop-in replacement for libopus in C or C++ code.
how_it_is_fast: It is a function-by-function port of libopus (names mirror the C sources) with hand-written SIMD kernels for CELT's hot loops: NEON on aarch64 and SSE/AVX/AVX2 on x86-64, chosen at run time through a cached feature probe. The kernels cover the KISS FFT radix-2/3/4/5 butterflies, the MDCT pre/post-rotation and TDAC fold, the pitch cross-correlation and inner products, band energy, renormalisation and stereo theta. The author attributes the 1.34-1.76x CELT encode lead to these kernels. libopus's float FFT and MDCT run its C code, since the build used no NE10. SILK is the fixed-point encoder, within a few percent of fixed-point libopus (0.97-1.11x). Decode reached 0.84-1.02x after profiling-driven fixes: integer divisions were removed from de-emphasis, per-band buffer zeroing was dropped, and the 16-tap SILK LPC synthesis loop was reordered so that only the newest tap sits on the loop-carried dependency chain.
when_to_use: Rust services that encode Opus at scale (music or mixed content at 64-256 kb/s, CELT mode) on aarch64 hosts such as Apple silicon. This is where the measured lead is largest: 1.34-1.76x libopus encode throughput.
Rust projects that want Opus with no C toolchain, system libopus or build.rs, for example to cross-compile to targets where linking C is awkward.
Reading and writing .opus files in Rust with correct pre-skip, end-trim and granule handling, including gapless round trips and zero-allocation looping playback (0.2.2).
VoIP encoders on SILK or hybrid at complexity 9-10, where the encoder ran 1.09-1.15x libopus's float build and 1.15x at complexity 10 in SILK wideband.
when_not_to_use: Decode-bound workloads. Decode is 0.84-0.92x of libopus in 9 of 10 measured rows, and the only win, stereo hybrid at 1.02x, decoded a bitstream about 6-10% smaller than libopus's.
C or C++ codebases. There is no C header or ABI, so calling it means writing and maintaining an FFI layer, and libopus itself is the simpler choice there.

x86-64 deployments that need proven speed. All published numbers are from one Apple M1 Pro. The AVX2 kernels run only on Linux x86-64 CI, and the README says the Rosetta runs used during development never reached them.

Low-complexity SILK encoding (complexity 0 or 5), where it is slightly slower than libopus (0.97x, 0.95x). The same applies to workflows needing an encoder bit-exact with libopus in CELT or hybrid: only SILK and the i16 API are byte-exact.

Very young code: first release on 2026-08-27, 3 stars, one maintainer, and a fork of a fork (rusty-opus 0.9.1, itself from restsend/opus-rs). Its own docs list several SIMD and rate-control defects fixed only recently.

integration.platforms: any Rust target. aarch64 uses NEON as baseline; x86-64 selects SSE, AVX or AVX2 at run time; other targets use scalar paths. CI covers Linux x86-64, Linux aarch64, macOS aarch64 and Windows x86-64.
integration.thread_safety: Encoders and decoders are independent owned values driven through &mut methods, one per stream. The only shared global state is the atomic CPU-feature cache. encode_parallel spawns scoped threads, each with its own encoder. Send and Sync guarantees are not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: settings, defaults (64 kb/s, complexity 9, constrained VBR), packet format and the i16 API match libopus behaviour, but the API is Rust-only with no C ABI, so existing libopus callers must be rewritten or wrapped.

gotchas: 'Pure Rust' does not mean unsafe-free. The SIMD kernels are unsafe fns using intrinsics, and PR #3 (2026-09-03, after the published measurements) fixed out-of-bounds reads in the NEON xcorr_kernel (when len == 0) and in the NEON short-prediction path of silk/nsq_del_dec.rs. The maintainer verified that encoder output stayed byte-identical.

Decoded float output can exceed plus or minus 1, as in libopus. Use decode_s16 or SoftClip before converting. encode_s16 declares 16-bit input depth and the float API declares 24-bit, so the two produce different packets for the same audio.

encode_parallel is not equivalent to a serial encode: the worst frame at a chunk boundary lands about 4 dB below serial, and workers are capped at one per 8 s of audio. The Ogg reader can only rewind to the start; there is no arbitrary seek.

The README says encode makes about ten short-lived allocations per frame (about 500 per second per stream), mostly in tonality analysis. 0.2.2 moved some of that scratch into encoder state, so measure before hosting hundreds of streams per process.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick opus-pure over its ancestors rusty-opus and opus-rs (both catalogued) when you need the Ogg layer, documented libopus interop (440-configuration sweep, byte-exact SILK) and the defect fixes its docs list, including the hybrid per-channel rate split and the aarch64 NEON kernel fixes. For decode-heavy Rust use, ruopus reports decode faster than libopus 1.6.1 (1.41-1.79x) on its own harness, and opuspp is the C++ option for a faster decoder. All of these come from different harnesses and machines, so cross-entry ratios are not directly comparable.
verified_claims_summary: The repo's own harness (reference/speed: rspeed vs cspeed.c) ran on an Apple M1 Pro on 2026-08-23 against static libopus 1.6.1 (sha256-pinned, CMake Release float build, NEON with runtime dispatch). It used 8 s of generated speech or music at 48 kHz, 20 ms frames, complexity 9, a fresh encoder per pass and the fastest of 12 passes; rustc and clang versions were not recorded. Encode ran 1.09-1.12x (SILK), 1.14-1.15x (hybrid) and 1.34-1.76x (CELT) of libopus's speed, and decode 0.84-0.92x except 1.02x for stereo hybrid. Each stack decodes its own packets, and the README text says the hybrid rows code 6-10% fewer bits than libopus and the SILK rows 6-11% more, so only the CELT rows (both within 1% of target) time equal work. The published table omits the delivered-bitrate column that run.sh prints and flags.
status_note: Active (0.2.2 on 2026-09-28, 19 commits, 15,710 crates.io downloads, one open PR) and BSD-3-Clause with no dependencies, so it is easy to adopt in Rust. The speed table predates the 0.1.0 import and has not been re-run for 0.2.2.
